content:
When we checked out the hardware of the VZMORE iX9 Max mini PC with an unboxing and a teardown in this first part of the review, we noted that the Intel Core Ultra 9 185H mini PC’s motherboard was identical to the one found in the GEEKOM IT13 Max. So in the more detailed Windows 11 Pro review, we’ve decided to focus on the main differences, notably the NVMe SSD, the wireless module, and cooling solution. The VZMORE mini PC also implements three power modes at 20W, 40W, and 65W, so we’ll run our usual benchmarks such as PCMark 10, 3DMark, and PassMark PerformanceTest 11 at different power levels, as well as measure fan noise and power consumption in different conditions.
